samples.summary: Read-only sheet mount still lets a signed-in viewer-role share-link visitor write comment threads/replies/resolutions into the CRDT root; the new YorkieStore.readOnly gate does not cover the comment mutators and no UI gate stands in front of them
samples.evidence: Vector: a visitor who has a Wafflebase account but is NOT a workspace member opens a viewer-role share link to a spreadsheet. shared-document.tsx:283 mounts SheetView readOnly={true}, so the store is new YorkieStore(doc, tabId, true) (sheet-view.tsx:1012). Selection still works in read-only, and the onSelectionChange handler at sheet-view.tsx:1128-1169 auto-opens the comment popover (setCommentPopoverOpen(true), line 1168) whenever the selected cell carries an unresolved thread - it has no readOnly check. The popover is then rendered at sheet-view.tsx:1719 with no readOnly prop, and CommentPopover.tsx:47 computes isReadOnly = currentUser === null, i.e. it only asks 'are you signed in?', never 'what is your share role?'. Because the visitor is signed in, commentAuthor is non-null (sheet-view.tsx:191) and CommentThreadCard renders the reply composer (CommentThreadCard.tsx:188) and the resolve toggle (line 107). Clicking them calls handleCommentReply / handleCommentResolve / handleCommentEdit / handleCommentDelete (sheet-view.tsx:921, 940, 967, 974), which call the RAW store: YorkieStore.addReply -> this.doc.update((root) => applyAddReply(ws, ...)) at yorkie-store.ts:1329, setThreadResolved at :1364, editComment at :1348, deleteComment at :1354. None of these consult the readOnly field this delta introduced, and sheets has no read-only store proxy (packages/sheets/src/store/readonly.ts is the datasource query-result store, not an access wrapper), so the write reaches doc.update and the next PushPull carries verb rw. With YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE unset the webhook refuses it (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:370, needWrite ? link.role === 'editor' : true), so the observable damage is the viewer's sync wedging - the exact failure this delta exists to remove, just via a different write. With the documented shadow-mode rollout option (YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE=false) the write PERSISTS, i.e. a viewer-role visitor mutates a document they hold read-only access to. Docs closes this same path (docs-comments-controller.ts:253 canComment = !readOnly && ..., and docs-view.tsx:695 passes readOnly to DocsCommentPopover), which is why I read the sheets case as a missed gate rather than a decision. Fix belongs in two places: pass readOnly into CommentPopover / gate the auto-open, and gate the comment mutators inside YorkieStore next to updateSelection so the store-level flag actually means what its new doc comment claims.

samples.summary: Both new constructors default readOnly = false, so the security-relevant flag fails open for any call site that omits it
samples.evidence: yorkie-store.ts:101 (readOnly = false) and yorkie-doc-store.ts:590 (constructor(doc, readOnly = false)). A future or refactored mount that forgets the third/second argument silently gets a store that publishes presence and (for sheets) grows the CRDT axis root, with no type error to catch it - packages/frontend has no tsc lane at all. There is already one production call site relying on the default, apply-imported-content.ts:224 (new YorkieDocStore(doc).setDocument(...)); that one is an authenticated owner-side import so it is currently fine, but it shows the default is load-bearing. The repo's own reasoning in packages/docs/src/store/read-only.ts (lines 6-19: allowlist readers, 'a list nobody remembers to extend fails open') argues for the opposite default. Suggest a required parameter, or a named factory for the writable case, so the permissive mode has to be asked for.

samples.summary: The docs store's readOnly is captured once at construction while the mount effect's dep list omits readOnly, so a post-mount role downgrade would keep publishing presence on the raw store
samples.evidence: docs-view.tsx:364 builds new YorkieDocStore(doc, Boolean(readOnly)) inside an effect whose deps are [didMount, doc] (line 581). If a surface ever renders DocsView with readOnly flipping false -> true without a remount (e.g. a permission/role refetch, a lock or an expiring share role), the store keeps readOnly=false and onCursorMove/publishResolvedLocalCursor keep issuing rw presence writes on the raw store, and initialize(..., readOnly) at line 367 likewise stays in its writable configuration. Not reachable today: the only readOnly-passing caller is SharedDocsLayout (shared-document.tsx:322,364), which derives it from resolved.role and mounts only after resolveShareLink settles, and the owner route (docs-detail.tsx:280) never passes it. Reported as a durability concern about where the authorization state is latched. Note SheetView already includes readOnly in its effect deps (sheet-view.tsx:1341), so the two mounts differ.
searchedFor: Read docs-view.tsx:330-581 (mount effect and dep list)

verdict.reason: Verified the absence at every hop. YorkieStore consults this.readOnly only in updateSelection (yorkie-store.ts:651) and ensureAxisOrder (:689); the comment mutators addThread/addReply/editComment/deleteComment/setThreadResolved (:1316, :1329, :1348, :1354, :1364) call doc.update with no guard. No UI gate stands in front: onSelectionChange auto-opens the popover with no readOnly check (sheet-view.tsx:1166-1168), the popover is rendered without a readOnly prop (sheet-view.tsx:1709-1729, unlike its !readOnly siblings at :1640/:1652/:1662), CommentPopover derives isReadOnly solely from `currentUser === null` (CommentPopover.tsx:47), and CommentThreadCard therefore renders the resolve toggle (:107) and reply composer (:188) for any signed-in visitor. Handlers handleCommentReply/Resolve/Edit/Delete (sheet-view.tsx:916-977) check only commentAuthor before hitting the raw store. I searched for counterexamples elsewhere and found none: no access wrapper for sheets (packages/sheets/src/store/readonly.ts is the datasource result store; the analogous wrapper exists only at packages/notes/src/store/read-only.ts), no canComment-style gate outside app/docs (docs-comments-controller.ts:253), and no viewer sync-mode restriction on the shared mount (shared-document.tsx:283, 1017-1025). In-lane and blocking: the enforced webhook gate is optional infrastructure — yorkie-auth.controller.ts:139-141 says method registration is a separate manual step and with none registered the endpoint never runs, while :126 designates the client-side read-only mounts as the layer that keeps this app from writing where it must not. With the webhook unregistered or in the documented YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE=false shadow mode, a viewer-role share-link visitor's comment writes persist into a document they hold read-only access to; with enforcement they are refused at PushPull (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:370) and wedge the viewer's sync.

mergedFrom.summary: READ_GATED_METHODS lets a viewer-role share token write: the AttachDocument change pack is applied under a read-only decision

finding.summary: `READ_GATED_METHODS` downgrades `AttachDocument` to a read check, so a share-link `viewer` can write arbitrary content by carrying a change pack in the attach itself
finding.evidence:
Before this change `checkAttribute` computed `needWrite = attr.verb === 'rw' || REVISION_READ_METHODS.has(method)`, so an `AttachDocument` (which Yorkie always sends with verb `rw`) required `link.role === 'editor'`. The new expression at yorkie-auth.controller.ts:332-334 is `REVISION_READ_METHODS.has(method) ? true : attr.verb === 'rw' && !READ_GATED_METHODS.has(method)` — with `READ_GATED_METHODS = new Set(['AttachDocument'])` (line 108), an attach is now authorized as a read, which `hasAccess` grants any valid viewer link (line 370: `return needWrite ? link.role === 'editor' : true`).

Attack: an anonymous holder of a viewer-role share link POSTs the token to `POST /auth/yorkie-token/share` (auth.controller.ts:82) to mint a `yorkie-share` token, reads the project public key out of any visitor's bundle, then builds a bare `yorkie.Client`, creates a local `Document`, applies arbitrary local changes, and calls `attach`. Yorkie pushes that change pack as part of the AttachDocument RPC; the webhook is consulted with verb `rw` but answers ALLOW because attach is read-gated, so the pack is applied. Detaching and re-attaching repeats it without bound, so the "one pack per attach" bound is not a practical limit — a viewer has effective write access to the document on a fully enforcing deployment.

The change explicitly acknowledges this (`docs/design/yorkie-auth-webhook.md` § Risks, the READ_GATED_METHODS comment, packages/backend/README.md:222), and the public-template-gallery gate `assertYorkieAuthEnforced` now rests on a bound that is narrower than the role it advertises. I could not confirm the residual is closed anywhere else: `PushPull` is the only remaining write gate and it is reached only *after* the attach has already been applied. Flagging because a role check that was previously enforced is now not, and the surface it protects (every viewer-shared document, and every public template document whose `previewToken` is handed to every visitor) is the one the rest

verdict.reason: The code is present exactly as claimed. yorkie-auth.controller.ts:108 defines READ_GATED_METHODS = new Set(['AttachDocument']), and lines 332-334 compute needWrite = REVISION_READ_METHODS.has(method) ? true : attr.verb === 'rw' && !READ_GATED_METHODS.has(method), so an AttachDocument arriving with verb 'rw' is authorized as a read; hasAccess line 370 then returns true for any valid share link regardless of role. The attack entry point is reachable and unauthenticated: auth.controller.ts:82-90 exposes POST /auth/yorkie-token/share with no guard, minting a yorkie-share token from any share token, and the controller's own doc comment (lines 120-130) states the webhook is the only place a viewer's write is refused, the frontend read-only mounts being 'a correctness boundary, not an access-control one'. I enumerated all AttachDocument/PushPull references and found no other guard on the attach-carried change pack; PushPull is reached only after the attach pack is applied. The repository itself documents the residual as open, not closed (docs/design/yorkie-auth-webhook.md:310-319; controller comment lines 99-106; yorkie-auth-enforcement.ts:15-19). I explicitly considered 'already-guarded' (no role filter exists at the token endpoint or elsewhere) and 'out-of-scope' (a documented, accepted upstream limitation is a rationale, not a mitigation); neither refutes it. This is a weakened access-control gate letting a share-link viewer obtain write effect, which is critical by impact under the security rubric.
